html:
Simón Iturri Patiño was a Bolivian mine owner known as the tin king, one of the richest men in the world in the early 1900s. His mines made tin the main export of Bolivia.

A man of mixed descent from the Cochabamba valley, he acquired a share in a mine near Llallagua in the 1890s and struck a rich vein of tin around 1900. As silver lost value, tin, needed for cans and machines, became Bolivia's great export. Patiño bought more mines and then smelters in Europe, controlling much of the world's tin trade. He lived abroad from the 1920s.

The three tin barons, Patiño, Hochschild and Aramayo, dominated Bolivia's politics. Miners lived in harsh conditions, and strikes were met with massacres. The revolution of 1952 took over their mines. The wealth of Potosí and of tin both left the country.
sum: Simón Iturri Patiño was a Bolivian mine owner known as the tin king, one of the richest men in the world in the early 1900s. His mines made tin the main export of Bolivia.
